newsitem.title: TURKEY: Two Turkish ministers to quit in Islamist row.
newsitem.headline: Two Turkish ministers to quit in Islamist row.

text.p: Two Turkish ministers from the conservative wing of the Islamist-led coalition on Saturday announced their resignations in a government dispute over planned curbs on Islamist activism.
"He will hand in his resignation to the prime minister shortly," an aide to Health Minister Yildirim Aktuna told Reuters.
Earlier, state-run Anatolian news agency quoted Trade and Industry Minister Yalim Erez as saying he would step down.

"Out of respect for myself and the Turkish people I will give my resignation to the prime minister," he said after 30 minutes of talks with Tansu Ciller, the deputy prime minister and leader of his True Path Party.
The two ministers had already expressed open opposition to the Islamist Welfare Party of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan for stalling on military demands for a crackdown on religious activism.

The National Security Council, chaired by President Suleyman Demirel, was to meet later on Saturday for talks expected to focus on army orders to restrict religious education, penalise Islamist dress and move against Islamist business.
Leading newspapers said Ciller had warned Erbakan on Friday she would pull out of government unless his party agreed to the military requests.
Before her meeting with Erbakan on Friday, Ciller denied a press report that she would withdraw her party from modern Turkey's first Islamist-led government.

The National Security Council meeting was likely to deal with a key army demand, opposed by the Welfare Party, that the state's secularist education be extended to eight years from five, media reports said.
The planned education reforms would marginalise religious secondary schools, breeding ground of future Islamists.
